tagline: Through the Modoc forest to Goose Lake and the Oregon line
intro: The Emigrant Trail byway links Tulelake and New Pine Creek through the Modoc National Forest and past Goose Lake. On Highway 139 north of Canby, the drive crosses mostly flat terrain through the forest on a two-lane road. The Federal Highway Administration highlights the byway’s forest roads, recreation areas and surviving emigrant-trail remnants.

During the gold rush, the Applegate-Lassen Cut-Off crossed the Black Rock Desert toward Goose Lake before its branches continued into California and southern Oregon. The Canby connection developed from an unimproved road toward Klamath Falls. The modern highway has its own history: in 1939, California authorized taking over the Canby-Oregon road if the U.S. Forest Service and Bureau of Public Roads built and paved it. By mid-1939, most of it was paved. By 1946, that section carried the Highway 139 number. The Highway 139 number was later adopted in the 1964 renumbering. Despite its inclusion in the state’s Freeway and Expressway System, it remained a two-lane road.

Traveling from Tulelake, follow 139 through the forest toward Canby, then 299 east to Alturas. Alturas stands at the meeting of the Pit River’s north and south forks. U.S. 395 leads north toward Goose Lake and New Pine Creek on the state line.

moments.title: Canby
moments.text: Canby’s main street is Highway 299, where the I’SOT religious community displays nativity scenes. The community lies in Modoc County, 17 miles west of Alturas, and its first post office opened in 1874. An older road is commemorated northwest of town by California Historical Landmark 111. Its inscription describes a traceable emigrant trail near Pit River-Happy Camp Road, with trees eight to ten inches thick growing in the former roadbed. Canby later served as a supply point for Big Lakes Logging Camp in the Adin Mountains, until the late 1940s.

moments.title: Goose Lake
moments.text: Goose Lake has carried a ferry and has also dried out completely. During high water, at least from 1908 to 1912, the ferry Lakeview carried passengers and cargo between Davis Creek and Lakeview. The railway reached Davis Creek in 1911; the port fell out of use as lake levels dropped and the railroad continued to Lakeview. This alkaline lake crosses the Oregon-California border. Its recorded dry periods include 1851 and 2013 through 2015, so a lake on the map does not establish present water conditions. When full, the lake reaches a maximum depth of 24 feet.

moments.title: New Pine Creek
moments.text: New Pine Creek sits on U.S. 395 at the Oregon-California boundary, east of Goose Lake. An 1868 surveying error placed part of the community in Oregon despite its position south of the intended 42nd-parallel boundary. Delegations from the two states discussed the error in 1984 but left its status unchanged. The name also required an adjustment: postal authorities rejected Pine Creek because another community already used it. The New Pine Creek post office opened in 1876. Goose Lake State Recreation Area lies west of the community, along Stateline Road near the lake.
